lines: A four-bit decoder with a latch: the four inputs are read as a number from 0 to 15 on a strobe, and the one output matching that number is driven low while the other fifteen are high.
The least significant bit of the number being decoded, worth one.
The second bit of the number being decoded, worth two. The maker's tooltip calls this the most significant bit, which it is not.
The third bit of the number being decoded, worth four.
The most significant bit of the number being decoded, worth eight. The maker's tooltip names this jack B, though the panel prints IN D.
A rising edge reads the four input bits and latches the number; between strobes the outputs hold what that number selected.
While this is high every output is driven high and the latched number is ignored.
0V while the latched number matches this output's own number and the inhibit input is low; 10V the rest of the time.
Note — A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
Note — Nothing reaches the outputs until a rising edge arrives at the strobe input; with nothing patched there the latched number stays at 0 and output S0 is the selected one.

lines: A four-bit binary up/down counter that can be preset to a number and that carries in and out for chaining.
A rising edge advances the count by one, up or down according to the UP/DOWN input.
While this is high the count is held at 0 and every Q output is at 0V.
Sets the direction: high counts up, low counts down. Unpatched it counts as low, so the counter runs backwards.
One bit of the number the counter is loaded with while PRESET EN. is high: P1 is worth one, P2 two, P3 four and P4 eight.
While this is high the count is forced to the number on the P inputs and the clock is ignored.
While this is high the clock is blocked and the count is held; patch the carry output of another CD4516 here to chain the two.
The least significant bit of the count, worth one.
The second bit of the count, worth two.
The third bit of the count, worth four.
The most significant bit of the count, worth eight.
0V at the end of the count — 15 going up, 0 going down — and 10V the rest of the time, so it goes low for one count in sixteen.
Note — A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
Note — The counter advances on the rising edge of the clock, despite the maker's tooltip on that jack reading "Negative edge triggered".

lines: Two four-input multiplexers sharing one pair of select inputs: each passes whichever of its four inputs the select number picks.
One of the four inputs into that multiplexer; it reaches the output while the select inputs name its number, counting I0 to I3.
The lower select input, worth one; together with S1 it picks which numbered input each multiplexer passes.
The upper select input, worth two; together with S0 it picks which numbered input each multiplexer passes.
Take this low to let that multiplexer through. While it is high that multiplexer's output is held at 0V.
10V while that multiplexer is enabled and its selected input is high, 0V otherwise.
Note — A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
Note — The two enable inputs work the other way round from the rest of the plugin: with nothing patched they count as low, which is the enabled state, and taking one high shuts that multiplexer off.
Note — S0 and S1 are not per-multiplexer; the number they set picks the same numbered input in both.
